lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: estimation and reasonableness

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: In 55,240, compare the value of the 5 in the ten-thousands place with the 5 in the thousands place.

steps: The first 5 represents 50,000 and the second 5 represents 5,000.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 2364 - 1786.
Round 986 to the nearest hundred and 29 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 8307 - 2856 = 5451. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 5300.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 5451 and the rounded estimate is 5400.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 5551 and the rounded estimate is 5400.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 5400.

items.prompt: A student evaluates 12 × [5 + (5 - 3)] + 2: “They multiply 12 by 5 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 64.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The student multiplied before evaluating (5 - 3); the innermost difference is 2, giving 86.
The work is correct; 64 is the value.
The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 87.
The grouping symbols do not affect the order; 64 is the value.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 5224333, the value of the 3 in the tens place is the same value as the value of the 3 in the ones place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The places are adjacent, so 30 is 100 times as much as 3.
The values are 30 and 3; 30 is 10 times as much as 3, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The values are 30 and 3; 30 is the same value as 3, so the student's comparison is correct.
The values are 30 and 3; 30 is 1/10 as much as 3.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Subtract 6 from 19, multiply the difference by 5, then add 37.”
Which phrase describes 21 + [3 × (14 - 8)] without evaluating it?
choices: Subtract 8 from 14, multiply the difference by 3, then add 21.
Subtract 8 from 14, add 3, then multiply the sum by 21.
Add 21 and 3, then multiply the sum by the difference of 14 and 8.
Multiply 3 by 14, add 21, then subtract 8.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Let E represent 3751 + 5772. Without evaluating, how does (3751 + 5772) + 749 compare with E?
choices: 749 less than E
748 greater than E
750 greater than E
749 greater than E

items.prompt: A supply cart has 90 boxes with 30 markers in each box and 29 loose markers. Which expression represents the total number of markers?
A team packs 47 crates with 29 bottles in each crate, adds 57 loose bottles, and then uses 72 bottles. How many bottles remain?
